authors: David Broska; Michael Howes
title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: PPI++ with partially labelled clusters. Design parameters are G, mean labelling probability mu_p and intraclass correlation of label indicators eta_p (eta_p=0 is independent unit labelling, eta_p=1 is whole-cluster labelling). Asymptotic variance V^PP = (1/(kappa^2 G mu_p)) (V_eps - V_epsZ^2/V_Z) with V_eps = V_Ys + (eta_p(1-mu_p)+mu_p) V_Yd, V_Z = (V_fs + eta_p V_fd)/(1-mu_p), V_epsZ = V_Yfs + eta_p V_Yfd (Appendix C, Eq 21). Simulation (209 designs) says spreading labels over many broadcasts gives lowest RMSE; at mu_p=0.05 whole-cluster labelling nearly doubles RMSE. NO cost model: Sec 2.6 says labelling inside a sampled cluster 'may cost less' and Sec 4 says combining the formulas with a cost model is future work. Superpopulation, iid clusters, unit-level mean; not design-based. No crossover cost ratio.

authors: Stephen W. Raudenbush
title: Statistical Analysis and Optimal Design for Cluster Randomized Trials
full_text_open: yes (open reading-list copy at Northwestern IPR)
what_it_holds: Optimal n per cluster with cost constraint (T monetary units, C1 per person and C2 per cluster), no covariate: Eq 9, which the paper says duplicates Cochran (p177). With a covariate: residual between- and within-cluster variances replace the raw ones; optimal n is given by Eq 24 as 'the solution to' an equation, to a close approximation (Appendix), so it may be implicit rather than the closed form m*sqrt((1-R2_w)/(1-R2_c)) [verify in Appendix]. Adjusted ICC is smaller than unadjusted. Example rho=.05, C2/C1=10: optimal n rises 14 to 19 with covariate (Tables 2 and 3). Section on aggregated (cluster-level) covariate, and p182 remark that collecting cluster-level covariates would increase C2. Equations were garbled in the extraction, so formulas not read.

authors: Reagan Mozer; Nicole E. Pashley; Luke Miratrix
title: Stratified Sampling for Model-Assisted Estimation with Surrogate Outcomes
what_it_holds: Finite-population design-based setting. Difference-type model-assisted estimator (surrogate mean difference plus stratified residual correction). Theorem 3.1 gives exact variance (expected sum of within-stratum residual variances weighted N_zk(N_zk-n_zk)/(N_z^2 n_zk), plus full-coding variance). Neyman-type allocation n_zk proportional to N_zk times residual SD, with capping. Budget is a count of coded units, no cost per unit. No clusters or two-stage. Not GREG; covariate adjustment left to future work. Relevant to regime B read as strata.

authors: Reagan Mozer
title: PPI is the Difference Estimator: Recognizing the Survey Sampling Roots of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: States PPI mean estimator = difference estimator and PPI++ = GREG (Eq 4). Section 3.1 contrasts finite-population (design-based) and superpopulation estimands. Mentions two-phase designs, post-stratification and Neyman allocation. Cluster sampling term does not appear. Reference list includes Kish (1965), Cassel-Sarndal-Wretman 1976, Sarndal-Swensson-Wretman 2003, Valliant-Dorfman-Royall 2000.

authors: Shinichiro Shirota
title: Design-Based Prediction-Powered Inference for Spatial Data
what_it_holds: Design-based PPI with census estimand. Prop 4 stratified variance Var = sum_h a_h S^2_{Y-tau f,h}, a_h = W_h^2(1-pi_h)/n_h, optimal tau* = sum a_h S_{Yf,h} / sum a_h S^2_{f,h}; tau* differs from pooled PPI++ value when H>1 because between-stratum component is removed by design. Prop 2 blocked design with one draw per block: gain over SRS only if between-block variance exceeds c_N times within-block variance, c_N=(n-1)/(N-n). Prop 3 Neyman-type allocation n_h proportional to N_h sigma_h. Simulated cluster design (8 centres x 8 pixels) with cluster-robust variance. No cost model; budget is label count. Two-stage not treated.
